faq.q: Does finding a signed transfer-on-death deed prove I can sell?
faq.a: No. A signed copy is a starting document, not a completed title review. Have the recording, property description, relevant events and any later instruments reviewed before signing as the owner.

faq.q: Where should I look for the recorded deed?
faq.a: The Texas State Law Library directs people to the county clerk where the property is located. For a Houston-area property, identify its actual county rather than assuming the mailing city determines the records office.

faq.q: Does a transfer-on-death deed erase a mortgage or lien?
faq.a: No. Texas Estates Code Chapter 114 addresses transfers subject to existing interests and encumbrances. Ask title professionals and your attorney what obligations affect the particular property and sale.

faq.q: Can Cash As-Is review the house while title questions are pending?
faq.a: You can describe the property and the unresolved document question for an offer evaluation. A purchase proposal does not determine ownership or replace the review needed for a valid closing.
